claim_scope: Same-host, same-GGUF, same-suite hipEngine vs llama.cpp HIP comparison at C1. llama.cpp rows are measured here; hipEngine rows are reused from the retained D7 closure and the current-main direct-leaf artifact and were not re-run in this packet. External diagnostic comparator, not a promoted hipEngine topline.
decision: hipEngine and llama.cpp HIP are at parity on Qwen3.8-27B Q4_K_M at C1. AR complete wall 9.807 vs 9.75 tok/s (+0.6%); MTP complete wall 15.609 vs 15.73 tok/s (-0.8%); MTP/AR 1.5916x vs 1.613x. hipEngine converts each speculative cycle slightly better (47.4% vs 43.5% complete-wall cycle efficiency). The single measured deficit is draft acceptance: 78.57% vs 90.16%, -11.6 points on the identical suite. This supersedes the as-published external comparison, which wrongly implied a 47-54% vs 70-77% engine gap; that spread is a target-size and timing-boundary artifact, not an engine gap.

model.architecture: qwen35, dense, 64 AR blocks + NextN block 64
model.note: Both engines drive the identical file. llama.cpp creates its MTP draft context against the same file's built-in NextN block, which is the provider hipEngine also uses.

commands: PYTHONPATH=. python3 scripts/mtp-bench.py --mode server --url http://127.0.0.1:8080 --model llama --prompts-file benchmarks/prompts/mtpbench-code-general-ja.jsonl --max-tokens 24 --temperature 0 --no-cache-prompt --out <arm>.json
limitations: hipEngine rows are reused from prior retained artifacts, not re-run inside this packet; a fully simultaneous A/B on one process lifecycle would be stronger.
KV dtype differs: hipEngine BF16, llama.cpp F16. This is the standing difference recorded in docs/MTP-LLAMACPP-PARITY.md and is not controlled here.
max_tokens=24 means prefill dominates the complete wall; decode-basis and complete-wall-basis ratios differ substantially (2.048x vs 1.613x for llama.cpp) and must not be mixed.
Single run per arm, no repeats; per-prompt decode rates were tightly clustered but no stdev is reported.
C1 only. No concurrency sweep was run against llama.cpp in this packet.
hipEngine working tree carried another owner's in-flight verifier-rowtile changes; hipEngine rows quoted here predate those changes.
next: Diff hipEngine NextN proposal against llama.cpp common/speculative.cpp draft-mtp to find the 11.6-point acceptance deficit: NextN priming and cursor synchronization, p_min handling, and per-position draft quality at K=2 and K=3.
